title: Inference deployment variant assessment
content:
Purpose and audience:
- Audience: Solutions Eng + customer architecture reviewers + product (dedicated/private PMs).
- Purpose: compare deployment variants for multi-tenant customer POC (retail+support use cases) and propose a recommended architecture that balances latency, cost predictability, data isolation, and rollout complexity.

Customer constraints (from kickoff):
- Regulated PII-sensitive interactions for a subset of retail flows (payment token masking required).
- Peak concurrent inference sessions: estimated 600 across global storefronts, 75% read-heavy, 25% chat/compose.
- Latency targets: 95th <= 250ms for short-text completions (<=256 tokens), tail tolerance up to 400ms for long form.
- Budget: prefer usage-based initially; customer open to reserved capacity if we can show predictable unit economics.
- Deployment preference: starts hosted, but wants a path to private-in-region for EU regulatory scope within 6 months.

High-level options considered:
1) Hosted-first (Redwood managed hosted API)
   - Pros: fastest to launch, no infra ops for customer, easy to iterate prompt sets, access to Redwood model catalog and auto-batching/caching. Good for early validation.
   - Cons: data residency concerns for regulated flows, potential noisy-neighbor latency variability at peak, less deterministic unit cost if usage spikes.

2) Dedicated-reserved (customer-specific GPU pool in Redwood infra)
   - Pros: predictable throughput and cost, isolated capacity reduces tail variance, can set autoscaling policies and burst options.
   - Cons: slower onboarding (~2–4 weeks), minimum commit needed; still not fully private (control plane in Redwood).

3) Private (VPC or on-prem)
   - Pros: full control over networking, KMS/HSM for keys, audit log locality, best for strict compliance.
   - Cons: longest lead time, ops maturity required from customer or Redwood-managed private offering; higher fixed cost.

Architectural patterns / unique options we recommend evaluating in POC:
- Hybrid routing with regulatory filters: route non-PII traffic to Hosted, route PII-sensitive flows to Dedicated or Private. Runtime policy evaluated in router/edge.
- Canary fallback / circuit-breaker: default to lower-cost hosted model variant; if latency or error rates exceed threshold, automatically failover to Dedicated instance with reserved capacity and stricter timeouts.
- Prefix/KV cache affinity: cache hot prefixes at edge workers (hosted) and seed Dedicated instances with warm KV snapshots to reduce cold-start costs during rollouts.
- QoS routing by tenant: allow VIP customers to be pinned to Dedicated; others get best-effort hosted.
- Burst strategy: combine Dedicated baseline + hosted burst for unexpected load; requires admission control and token-bucket shaping.

Trade-offs (short bullets, tech + business):
- Latency: Private ~ Dedicated < Hosted (median), but Hosted can achieve low median with smart batching; tail depends on multi-tenancy.
- Cost predictability: Dedicated (reserved) best, Hosted usage-based worst for predictable budgeting unless combined with committed spend.
- Compliance: Private > Dedicated > Hosted; however encryption-in-transit and CMK integration can improve Hosted compliance posture for many customers.
- Ops complexity: Hosted least, Private most.
- Time-to-value: Hosted fastest (days), Dedicated medium (weeks), Private longest (weeks->months).

Rough capacity & perf assumptions used for POC sizing (notes/estimates — validate with measurements):
- Model: 7B causal decoder baseline (float16 / int8 quant candidate).
- Throughput per A100-like GPU: ~18–25 tokens/sec median for chat patterns at batch sizes tuned for 50–150ms latency. H100 improves throughput ~1.4x.
- Target concurrency map: 600 concurrent sessions => steady-state token throughput ~45k tokens/sec (assumes avg 75 tokens/session/minute) — implies ~3–4 A100 equiv for median load if using batching aggressively; add reserve buffer for tails and canary.
- Cost back-of-envelope: hosted baseline $X per million tokens (use pricing sheet); Dedicated reserved reduces $/token by ~20–40% depending on commit.

Operational controls and observability we will implement in the POC:
- Per-route latency and per-token cost near-real-time dashboards.
- Alerting: 95th latency, error rate, congested queue depth, KV cache hit-rate.
- Rollouts: A/B canary by traffic percentage + automatic rollback on quality regressions (eval harness hooked to prompt set).
- Audit and data retention knobs: configurable retention (30/90/365 days) for Private/Dedicated; Hosted defaults to 30 days.

Open technical risks and mitigations:
- Cold-start tail: mitigate with warm pools and KV snapshot seeding; explore micro-batching warmers.
- Model variant divergence: need eval sets tied to customer prompts; run evals on both host/dedicated variants before switching.
- Cross-region routing complexity: use geo-aware edge with region pins for EU-sensitive flows.
- KMS integration for Private workflow: prototype key rotation and HSM signing flow in lab cluster.

Proposed POC plan (6–8 week timeline):
Week 0–1: Align on scope, finalize traffic profile, decide sample prompt set for quality evals.
Week 1–3: Launch Hosted-first baseline for all traffic; collect perf/quality metrics; implement prefix cache and basic routing rules.
Week 3–5: Stand up Dedicated reserved pool sized to 50% of peak; implement hybrid routing rules (regulatory filters + canary).
Week 5–6: Run degradation scenarios (burst, network partition) and verify automatic fallback/circuit-breakers.
Week 6–8: Work on Private in-region proof-of-concept (VPC link + KMS) for EU-sensitive flows; handoff checklist for Private readiness.

Success criteria for POC:
- Meets 95th latency SLO <=250ms for target short-form flows in at least two of three deployment modes (hosted with tuning, dedicated, private lab).
- Cost per effective token within agreed budget (<20% variance from projection).
- Demonstrated regulatory data path for PII-sensitive flows with audit logs and KMS integration.
- Failover tested: automatic switch from hosted -> dedicated during simulated host congestion with <1% lost requests.

Checklist for deployment decision meeting with customer:
- [ ] Confirm which flows are PII-sensitive and require region-residency.
- [ ] Approve initial hosting for non-PII flows (hosted) and timeline for EU private pilot.
- [ ] Sign off on Dedicated commit range (min/max) for reserved baseline.
- [ ] Accept runbooks for failover and incident response.
- [ ] Agree on eval prompt set and quality thresholds.

Open questions for customer / internal follow-ups:
- What is the absolute max monthly token usage if marketing campaign spike occurs? (we need an upper bound for commit sizing)
- Are there any legal constraints on log forwarding to Redwood-managed services?
- Will customer accept Redwood-managed KMS in hosted for the interim, or require customer KMS from day 1?
- Do we have a preferred list of third-party PCI/HSM vendors for the Private offering?

Immediate next steps (owner assignments):
- Aisha: schedule architecture review with customer + legal (by 2026-02-20).
- Maya: prepare a quick Hosted baseline runbook and measurement dashboard template (by 2026-02-26).
- Liam: size Dedicated config options (commit tier proposals) and cost scenarios (by 2026-02-24).
- Priya: prototype KMS/HSM key rotation flow in lab (by 2026-03-05).

Notes (disorganized):
- customer cares a lot about audit trails — include sample audit record format in next doc.
- consider offering a "sovereign region pilot" with reduced retention and stricter TLS cipher suites.
- TODO: validate throughput numbers on H100 cluster; might reduce required GPUs by ~25%.

End of doc (working draft).

# informal sign-off
- +1 from SEs on hybrid routing approach as minimum viable path for this customer; still need legal sign-off for hosted interim.
- Marking this as draft until we complete Hosted baseline metrics and customer confirms PII flow map.
